faq: Can my review data be moved?
Often, if your old review tool lets you export and the new one lets you import. Reviews must be genuine ones left by real customers. We never create, edit or buy reviews, in line with platform rules.
What if an app does not exist on the new platform?
We look for a close match or a built-in feature, and tell you what you gain and lose. Sometimes a small custom piece makes sense, which we quote separately before building anything.
Do I pay for the apps myself?
Yes. App subscriptions are billed by each app maker to your account. We list the plan we chose and the monthly cost before installing, so you can say no to anything that does not earn its place.
Will tracking and ad pixels be reconnected?
Basic analytics and ad pixels can be added here. For a full review with event tracking and testing, use the Analytics and tracking services, which go much deeper.

desc:
App and integration replacement for store migrations is the work of finding every tool your old store relied on and setting up the right equivalent on the new platform. Ecom Swift LLC reconnects reviews, email, shipping, accounting and more, then tests each one with real orders.

## What is app and integration replacement?

App and integration replacement means listing the extra tools attached to your store, deciding which ones still make sense and setting them up again after a platform move. Apps are add-ons built by other companies. Integrations are the links that pass data between your store and other systems, such as an accounting package or a shipping service.

Apps almost never transfer with the store. A review widget on the old platform is a separate product, and the new platform may have a different version of it, a built-in feature or nothing at all.

## Why the tool stack decides whether launch day goes smoothly

A store feels like one thing to a shopper, but behind the scenes it is a chain of connected tools. Orders flow to accounting, subscribers flow to email, parcels flow to a carrier. If one link is missing after the move, the damage is quiet at first. Invoices stop appearing, abandoned-cart emails stop sending and customers stop getting tracking messages.

Many owners also discover that they pay for tools they no longer use. A migration is the best moment to clean this up, because you are already making a decision about each one.

## How it affects revenue and workload

Some tools earn money directly. Email flows bring back shoppers who left items in the cart. Review stars on product pages help buyers feel safe. Loyalty programs encourage a second purchase. Losing any of these at launch means a dip you could have avoided.

Other tools save time. Automatic accounting entries, label printing and support chat all remove manual work. When they are reconnected and tested before launch, your team keeps its normal rhythm. When they are forgotten, someone ends up copying data by hand for weeks.

## What a good reconnection includes

- A full inventory of the apps and scripts on the old store, including ones nobody remembers installing.
- A decision for each tool: keep, replace with a similar app, use a built-in feature, or retire.
- Email lists and sign-up forms moved, with consent status respected.
- A reviews tool connected, with existing reviews imported where the tool supports it.
- Accounting and shipping tools linked to the new store.
- Support chat or help desk set up on the new storefront.
- Loyalty or subscription apps configured with the rules you want.
- Tracking and ad pixels checked so reporting continues.
- Test orders sent through every connected tool.
- A written comparison of what each tool cost before and what it costs now.

## What we do

We begin with a list. We read your current store, note every app and script, and ask you which ones you actually use. Then we check what exists on the new platform and write a short recommendation for each tool.

After you approve the plan, we install and configure the chosen tools in your own account. Where data can move, such as an email list, we move it. Where it cannot, we explain what will start fresh. Larger packages add more tools, a custom connection built with webhooks or Zapier, support and chat tools, and a handover document.

Finally we place test orders and follow each one through the chain: payment, email, label, accounting entry. Anything that breaks gets fixed before you go live.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a note of which tools earn money and which only save time.
- Check each app's monthly fee before you install it.
- Prefer a built-in feature when it does the same job.
- Test with a real order, not only a settings page.
- Keep your old tool accounts open until the new ones are proven.

**Avoid:**
- Installing three apps that do the same thing.
- Reconnecting every old tool by habit.
- Giving apps wider permissions than they need.
- Leaving old tracking codes running on the new store.
- Cancelling an old subscription before you have exported its data.

## Who this is for

A shop owner leaving a platform where six or seven apps ran the daily routine. A seller who wants to cut monthly costs while moving. A growing brand that needs email, reviews and accounting working together on day one, without hiring a developer.

## How to get started

Tell us which platform you are leaving and which one you are moving to. Send a list of the tools you remember, or give us a staff or collaborator user on the old store so we can see the installed apps ourselves.

Apps and plans are bought in your own accounts, so you stay in control of cost and ownership. We do not need your passwords. For tools that require a login, you can create a team seat for us and remove it when the job ends.
